discovery: The unitarity method and on-shell techniques for scattering amplitudes, enabling precision predictions for collider physics

nominees.name: Zvi Bern
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

nominees.name: Lance J. Dixon

nominees.name: David A. Kosower
nominees.affiliation: Institut de Physique Théorique, CEA Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Theoretical particle physics / quantum field theory
motivation: Bern, Dixon and Kosower showed that loop-level scattering amplitudes in gauge theories can be built directly from on-shell tree amplitudes through unitarity cuts, without Feynman diagrams or off-shell Lagrangian machinery. The unitarity method revealed unexpected simplicity in quantum field theory and made previously intractable multi-leg next-to-leading-order QCD calculations routine. Its descendants, automated in generalized-unitarity codes, now supply the precision Standard Model backgrounds on which Higgs measurements and new-physics searches at the LHC depend. The same ideas uncovered the double-copy relation between gauge theory and gravity, sharpened our understanding of ultraviolet behaviour of supergravity, and today give high-order post-Minkowskian predictions for gravitational-wave sources. On-shell methods have also transformed effective field theory, giving direct ways to classify operators and constrain physics beyond the Standard Model. This is a rare formal advance with deep, measurable impact on experiment.
